kynurenic: Pertaining to, or designating, an acid obtained from the urine of dogs. By decomposition the acid yields a nitrogenous base (called kynurin) and carbonic acid. [Written also cynurenic.]
kyke: To look steadfastly; to gaze. (old) [Written also kike, keke.] This Nicholas sat ever gaping upright, As he had kyked on the newe moon. Chaucer.
kyanol: (a) Aniline. (old) (b) A base obtained from coal tar. Ure.
kyloes: The cattle of the Hebrides, or of the Highlands. [Scot.] Sir W. Scott.
kythe: To make known; to manifest; to show; to declare. [Obs: or Scot.] For gentle hearte kytheth gentilesse. Chaucer. | To come into view; to appear. [Scot.] It kythes bright . . . because all is dark around it. Sir W. Scott.
kyriology: The use of literal or simple expressions, as distinguished from the use of figurative or obscure ones. Krauth-Fleming.
kydde: imp. of Kythe, to show. (old) Chaucer. Note: Spenser erroneously uses kydst to mean "knowest."
kymographic: Of or pertaining to a kymograph; as, a kymographic tracing.
kyack: A pack sack to be swung on either side of a packsaddle. [Western U. S.]
kyrielle: A litany beginning with the words. "Kyrie eleison." Shipley.
kyrieeleison: 1. (R. C. Ch.) Greek words, meaning "Lord, have mercy upon us," used in the Mass, the breviary offices, the litany of the saints, etc. Addis & Arnold. 2. The name given to the response to the Commandments, in the service of the Church of England and of the Protestant Episcopal Church.
ky: Kine. [Scot.] See Kee, Kie, and Kine.
kyar: Cocoanut fiber, or the cordage made from it. See Coir.
kyriolexy: The use of literal or simple expressions, as distinguished from the use of figurative or obscure ones. Krauth-Fleming.
kyriological: Serving to denote objects by conventional signs or alphabetical characters; as, the original Greek alphabet of sixteen letters was called kyriologic, because it represented the pure elementary sounds. See Curiologic.
kyanize: To render (wood) proof against decay by saturating with a solution of corrosive sublimate in open tanks, or under pressure.
kymograph: An instrument for measuring, and recording graphically, the pressure of the blood in any of the blood vessels of a living animal; -- called also kymographion.
